name: חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ
gloss: Yahweh has reckoned; or Yahweh has regarded
summary: A Levite name, borne by about a dozen men from David's time to Nehemiah's: a son of Jeduthun among the temple musicians (1Ch 25:3, 19), a Hebronite set over Israel west of the Jordan “for all the work of Yahweh and the service of the king” (1Ch 26:30), the ruler of the Levites in David's census of officers (1Ch 27:17), a Merarite in the line of Ethan the singer (1Ch 6:30), a chief of the Levites at Josiah's passover (2Ch 35:9), a Merarite who came up with Ezra and was given charge of the gold and silver for the house of God (Ezr 8:19, 24), a ruler of half the district of Keilah who repaired the wall (Neh 3:17), one who sealed the covenant (Neh 10:12), a head of the Levites in Nehemiah's day (Neh 12:24), and a priest of the house of Hilkiah (Neh 12:21). The name is the verb חָשַׁב with יָהוּ: “Yahweh has reckoned” or “has regarded”, as the psalmist says “Adonai thinks on me (יַחֲשָׁב לִי)” (Psa 40:18). Scripture does not explain the name.

evidence.note: Among the sons of Jeduthun, “חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ and Mattithiah, six”.
“Of the Hebronites, חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ and his brothers … over Israel beyond the Jordan westward, for all the work of Yahweh.”
One of twelve chiefs of the priests and Levites given charge of the silver and gold for the house of God.
“I am poor and needy; Adonai thinks on me (יַחֲשָׁב לִי)”: the root with a divine subject and the person regarded.
Those “who esteem (חֹשְׁבֵי) his name” are remembered before Yahweh.

note: Takes h.gr.ah (15 tokens, spellings חֲשַׁבְיָהוּ and חֲשַׁבְיָה). TIPNR numbers by the English verses: Hashabiah@1Ch.6.45 is 1Ch 6:30 in the Hebrew. TIPNR has no separate records for the Hashabiah of Ezr 8:24, Neh 10:12, Neh 11:15 and Neh 12:24; their tokens are tagged through TIPNR's own merging. The reading “Yahweh has reckoned/regarded” takes the first element as the qal perfect; no verse gives the meaning.
